title: BillingProvider never mounted — BillingContext is an unreachable stub
detail: src/contexts/BillingContext.jsx exports BillingProvider and useBilling, but BillingProvider is never imported or mounted anywhere in the app tree (App.jsx:462–470 confirms). The stub returns Infinity credits and a no-op deduct(). All credit gating is server-side. Client UI cannot reflect credit status or show remaining-search counts to users without wiring this up.
fix_hint: Mount BillingProvider inside AuthProvider in App.jsx once Phase 2 ships. Wire to /api/credits GET. Expose credit balance in Header nav.

title: SettingsContext / SettingsProvider never mounted or consumed
detail: src/contexts/SettingsContext.jsx wraps useSettings in a context and exports SettingsProvider + useSettingsContext, but neither is imported or used anywhere. All settings consumers call useSettings() directly from App.jsx with prop-drilling. The file is dead.
fix_hint: Either delete the file, or mount SettingsProvider in App.jsx (replacing the useSettings() call) and migrate consumers to useSettingsContext().

title: Home screen empty-state checks settings.europeanaKey — implementation detail in view
detail: App.jsx:444 renders a 'Visit Settings to enable supplemental sources' banner conditioned on !settings.europeanaKey. This leaks key-management internal knowledge into the home-screen presentation layer. When europeanaKey is dropped (once the backend env key is provisioned, per defaults.js TODO), this check will silently show/hide incorrectly.
fix_hint: Derive a hasAllKeyedSources boolean from adapter state or settings, and use that instead of the raw europeanaKey check.

title: ThemeStrip swatches have no text labels — color-only affordance
detail: src/components/Layout.jsx:210–218 renders theme swatches as 20px colored squares with only a `title` attribute tooltip. Screen readers get no useful label; colorblind users cannot distinguish Cream from Blue-grey. The title is shown on hover but not persistently accessible.
fix_hint: Add aria-label={t.label} to each swatch button. Optionally show the label text on focus or below the active swatch.

title: Stale comment in SettingsPanel claims slider/search-toggles live there
detail: src/components/Panels.jsx:380–382 comment says 'Synonym, Semantic, relevance slider, Author search AND Result layout all live in the always-visible SearchControls'. This is accurate — they were moved in v.31/v.36/v.37 — but reading the code without context the comment implies these existed in SettingsPanel, which is confusing. The comment is essentially a migration note that should be cleaned up.
fix_hint: Remove the migration comment. The SearchControls location is documented in the wiki.

title: Apple and Microsoft OAuth providers rendered as disabled dead UI for all users
detail: src/components/Layout.jsx:9–11 defines PROVIDERS array with Apple (active: false) and Microsoft (active: false). These render as greyed 'soon' items in the sign-in dropdown for every unauthenticated user. Only Google (active: true) is wired. The dead items create visual noise and false expectations.
fix_hint: Remove Apple/Microsoft from PROVIDERS array until they are implemented. Re-add when the OAuth integration ships.

title: LibraryPanel uses native confirm() for destructive clear-all action
detail: src/components/Panels.jsx:499 uses confirm(`Remove all ${items.length} items from your library?`). Native browser confirm() is unstyled, inaccessible (cannot be focused/trapped by screen readers in the same way), and inconsistent with the rest of the UI aesthetic.
fix_hint: Replace with an inline confirmation UI (e.g., a two-step button: 'Clear all' → 'Are you sure? Confirm') consistent with the existing design system.

title: useSearch has no AbortController — stale adapter responses can land in state after a new search
detail: src/hooks/useSearch.js:44 uses activeAdapters.forEach(async adapter => { … setSectionStates(prev => …) }). If the user fires a second search before a slow adapter from the first search resolves, that adapter's response will patch the new search's sectionStates via setSectionStates(prev => …). The prev-based merge means the stale response overwrites the correct loading:true state with stale results from the previous query.
fix_hint: Add a searchId ref (useRef(0)), increment on each search() call, and check inside each async callback that the current searchId matches before calling setSectionStates.

title: SettingsContext is exported but never mounted or consumed — duplicate of F-301
detail: See F-301. Filed separately against hooks.useSettings to capture the dependency relationship: SettingsContext.jsx imports useSettings but is itself dead. Both records point to the same root cause.

title: DEFAULT_THEME exported from themes.js but never imported by useTheme
detail: src/constants/themes.js:49 exports DEFAULT_THEME = 'tan'. src/hooks/useTheme.js never imports it — instead hardcodes LIGHT_DEFAULT = 'tan' and DARK_DEFAULT = 'oled' at lines 4–5. If DEFAULT_THEME is changed, useTheme will silently remain on 'tan'.
fix_hint: Import DEFAULT_THEME in useTheme.js and use it as LIGHT_DEFAULT, eliminating the duplicated constant.

title: GoldSetHarness stores data in bare localStorage keys outside the opencite: namespace
detail: src/components/admin/GoldSetHarness.jsx:16–27 uses localStorage.getItem('opencite_gold_queries') and localStorage.getItem('opencite_test_runs') directly, bypassing the namespaced storage utility (lib/storage.js). These keys use underscores (not the opencite: colon-separated namespace). This risks key collision with other apps, breaks storage.remove(), and is inconsistent with the rest of the app.
fix_hint: Replace localStorage.getItem/setItem calls with storage.get/set('gold_queries') and storage.get/set('test_runs') from lib/storage.js.

title: No client-visible credit balance — free users cannot see how many searches remain
detail: BillingContext is a stub (F-300) so there is no client-side credit counter. The server gates usage at /api/search, but the UI gives no feedback before or after exhaustion. Free users (20 searches/month) have no visibility into their remaining balance until a server 402 (v0.37 plan, not yet shipped).
fix_hint: Wire BillingProvider to a /api/credits GET on sign-in; surface remaining credits in the Header nav (e.g., near the Plans button).

title: AuthModal has no focus trap — keyboard users can tab behind the overlay
detail: src/components/Layout.jsx:264–325 renders AuthModal as a fixed full-screen div overlay. There is no focus trap: keyboard users can Tab behind the modal to the main page while the overlay is open. This is an accessibility failure (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.2).
fix_hint: Use a focus-trap library (e.g., focus-trap-react) or implement a manual focus trap: on mount, move focus to the first button inside the modal; on Tab/Shift-Tab, cycle within modal children only.

title: LibraryPanel uses native confirm() for clear-all
detail: See F-306. Filed against components.Panels for the module binding.

title: Book-chapter group header JSX duplicated across SourceSection and UnifiedResultList
detail: The parent-work header block (chapter count badge, year, title h3, editors, publisher) is reproduced nearly verbatim at SourceSection.jsx:75–103 and UnifiedResultList.jsx:136–164 — approximately 30 lines of JSX each. Any change to the visual design must be applied in both places.
fix_hint: Extract a <BookGroupHeader group={group} /> component in a shared file (e.g., components/BookGroupHeader.jsx) and import it in both SourceSection and UnifiedResultList.

title: PricingPanel currentPlan hardcoded 'free' — paying subscribers always see Free as current
detail: src/components/Panels.jsx:190 has defaultProps currentPlan='free'. App.jsx:299 passes no currentPlan prop, so it always defaults to 'free'. Paying subscribers will see the 'Current' badge on the Free card regardless of their actual subscription tier.
fix_hint: Wire currentPlan to the actual user plan from BillingContext (once live) or from the server session. Pass the resolved plan as a prop from App.jsx.
